_note: ENG-10/GAME-10a: one Foamer spec per type. `test` is the shared base spec every type starts from (the name is kept: the F01 tests read it directly). `types` holds one entry per type with only what differs from the base: its rig id in data/foamer-rigs.json and its attacks. An attack's `token` is the director pool it draws from; its `needs` are parts that must still be attached; its `range`, when it has one, is how far its reach is measured to (default: an attack with a melee token uses the base attackRange, one with a ranged token the preferred distance). The three *DistanceMetres fields belong to the base so every spec has them; only a ranged type reads them: the distance at which it stops walking in and keeps the ring (throwRangeMetres), the distance it tries to keep and throws from (preferredDistanceMetres), and the distance it backs off to when the player closes inside it (retreatDistanceMetres).

partDamage._note: Per part kind. hpShare: the part's health as a share of the Foamer's (at least minHp). hit: multiplies dart damage to the part. total: share of that damage that also comes off the Foamer's health. CONTENT-PLAN 3.1 and 3.2.

catastrophic._note: Pop when the damage from popTypes dart types in the last window seconds is at least share of max health. No starter dart type pops (Paul, 2026-11-01): heavier darts and blaster mods add theirs.

chunk._note: GAME-09b: the chunk finish. A blaster or mod with a chunk block, a hit inside its rangeMetres, qualifies when the killing shot's own damage on this Foamer inside the window above is at least minShare of max health, and the rig's tier is in tiers or the Foamer is already finishable (finishWeakened). Then carveRadius is carved as a sphere at the shot's mean hit point, up to debrisMax foam chunks burst out of the hole, and it goes down with the hole in it, pushed chunk.push times the ragdoll's kill push. Pops are unchanged.

finisher._note: GAME-07. weakenShare: when health first falls to or below this share of the max, the Foamer is finishable and staggers for weakenStaggerTime instead of stagger.time (a part break still gives the short stagger). reach: melee finishers work this far from the eye. coneCos: the view cone's cosine, the aim must be inside it. total: the finisher's lasting time. turnTime: the share of total the view spends turning onto the Foamer. CONTENT-PLAN 3.1 and 3.2: the finisher always pops.

ragdoll._note: ENG-12. density in kg/m^3 for the part cuboids. damping slows the fall to a limp, heavy foam feel. keepStride: share of a walking Foamer's speed its parts keep when it dies (the stride feeds the fall without deciding it). killSpeed: the killing shot tips the Foamer over about its feet, away from the shooter: every part gains this speed in m/s along the shot's horizontal direction, scaled by its height over the top of the body (feet barely move, the top moves most), so it falls without being thrown. limits: hinge range in radians about the part's local x axis, per part kind, measured from the pose it had when it went down (negative bends forward).

handicaps._note: GAME-11. someLegsSpeed: ground speed with some legs gone but still enough to walk. noLegsSpeed: with none left. noHeadTurnRate: turn rate scale with no head. fallBelowLegs: a living Foamer left with fewer legs than this falls over. crawlSpeed: crawl speed as a share of the rig speed. crawlLength: the lying capsule's length as a share of the rig height. fall: the fall is an inverted pendulum about the foot it still stands on, a in radians from upright and a'' = (gravity / pivotHeight) * sin(a). startTilt: the tilt it starts from, so it tips at once. proneTilt: the tilt it lands at. sideShare: share of the tilt that is roll toward the lost leg, the rest is forward pitch. bounce: share of the landing angular speed it bounces back with, once. settle: seconds at rest after the bounce before it crawls.

F05._note: GAME-10b: the Darter. attackRange is its bite; the charge line and speed are in charge, and the brain reads rangeMetres. The chest and brow plates shrug off darts and carve little; the orange back weakpoint takes extra. No upright attack besides the charge: with no legs it is prone, so only bite is left.

charge._note: GAME-10b: the charge. speed m/s, metres the longest run, rangeMetres where a charge may start, holdMetres the ring it circles on without a token (so it charges from range), telegraphSeconds the scrape before it (stops, head down, dust), wallStunSeconds the stagger after a wall (back open), playerStunSeconds how long a player it runs into cannot move. plateStopsShield and plateArcDeg: a shield charge into the front plates bounces off instead of staggering the Darter.

armour._note: GAME-10b: per part id. damage multiplies the kind's hit multiplier; carve scales the dart carve radius (the plate chips slowly).

F03._note: GAME-10d: the Swarmer. Weak point: none. Health 2 comes from its rig (it pops in one or two hits). nibble is its whole attack: a short windup, hit and run. pack is how many a pack spawn makes; the swarm ring and gaps are in data/ai.json pack. The type reads its own speed and health from the rig.

F04._note: GAME-10e: the Blocker. Holds a shield wall: slots side by side at slots.holdMetres, a volley over the shield with the ranged token. The shield is armour on the shield part, but only across its arcDeg front: a side or back dart takes full damage, and a staggered Blocker has the shield down. shieldChargeTime is the stagger the player shield charge leaves it in (a longer one than the base). turnRate 1.4 rad/s, the Darter's (review: at 5 it faced a strafing player within a second, so flanking could not work).

slots._note: GAME-10e: the shield wall. Blockers walk to a line across the player at holdMetres, one slot each spacingMetres apart; an index past the ends of the line spreads the wall.

armour._doc: GAME-10e: the shield. A front dart chips it slowly and does almost nothing; arcDeg is how much of the front it covers. Out of the arc, or with the shield down (stagger), full damage.

attacks._note: GAME-10e: range pins the volley's reach, so a Blocker on its slot (the hold distance) is inside it and fires over the shield.

line._note: GAME-10e: the line the range spawns for the F04 type choice, so one press shows the wall. inboundSteps: a blocked slot slides outward this many slots before the member is skipped.

F07._note: GAME-10f: the Brawler. A heavy that walks in like the F01 and punches up close (the melee brain), and between leap.minMetres and leap.maxMetres, off cooldown, crouches, leaps an arc and lands a shockwave ring the player jumps or dashes through. Health 45 and speed 2.4 come from the rig. Weak point: none (CONTENT-PLAN 3).

leap._note: GAME-10f: the leap slam. It crouches (crouchSeconds, the telegraph) when the player is between minMetres and maxMetres and the cooldown is up, then flies an arc (arcMetres high at speed m/s) to a point landShortMetres short of where the player was, and lands a shockwave. cooldownSeconds runs from the start of the crouch. Both legs gone: no leap, it crawls as the F01 does; an arm gone does not stop it.

shockwave._note: GAME-10f: the ring the landing sends out. It grows from the landing point at speed m/s out to radius metres; the band is thickness metres wide (a player the outer edge reaches while the inner edge has not passed them). A grounded player in the band as it passes loses damage once; one in the air (a jump) or dashing takes none. tubeMetres is the drawn torus's tube radius.

attacks._note: GAME-10i: the sword swing. It needs the sword (the left fist stays free); with the sword gone it falls to the left-fist punch below. Its range is pinned per attack, so the fallback punch still measures to the spec's attackRange (1.7).

F09._note: GAME-10g: the Crawler. A heavy turret walker: keep-distance like the Roamer (the F02 brain), holding at preferredDistanceMetres. Health 40 and speed 1.8 come from the rig. The gun is the weak point (weakpoint); with the gun gone, or both barrels, it cannot fire and stomps. Look (CONTENT-PLAN 3.4): deep orange body, purple legs, lime gun.

pellets._note: GAME-10g stage 2: one burst. count pellets, one every intervalSeconds, each aimed at the eye with a random turn of plus/minus spreadDeg from a seeded PRNG (seed), never Math.random().

weakpoint._note: GAME-10g: CONTENT-PLAN 3.1, the gun is the weak point. GAME-10j: this became the parts list (the F10's jets are two parts).

attacks._note: range is the distance it fires from, a little outside the ring it keeps (the F06's pattern): the brain parks on preferredDistanceMetres, so an unpinned ranged range would sit exactly on it. needs the gun; a barrel too (canStream in src/foamers/pellet.ts).

F08._note: GAME-10h: the Trawler. A heavy slow tank: keep-distance like the Roamer (the F02 brain), holding at preferredDistanceMetres 12 and firing its wall of balls from up to throwRangeMetres. Health 80 and speed 0.9 come from the rig. The two arm launchers are the weak points (wall.launchers, wall.weakpointMultiplier); with one gone the wall is that launcher's half, with both gone it cannot fire and stomps. Look (CONTENT-PLAN 3.4): deep lime body, purple shields (the shoulder nubs and the drum), orange launchers.

wall._note: GAME-10h stage 2: the wall of foam balls. ballsPerLauncher from EACH launcher, spacingMetres apart, so the row is about 6 m wide. Balls are slow (speed) and flat (gravity 0) so the wall can be read, and burst on any geometry. gapBalls side-by-side balls are left out at a position picked by a seeded PRNG (seed, mixed with the wall's number), never at the row's ends, so a player who reads it steps through. Not parryable: the wall has its own material, not BALL_MATERIAL (CONTENT-PLAN gives F08 no P). Each launcher owns its half of the row and is a weak point (weakpointMultiplier). The starting numbers are proposals for Paul to tune. See src/foamers/wall.ts.

attacks._note: range pins the wall's firing distance a little outside the ring it keeps (the F09 stream's pattern): the brain parks on preferredDistanceMetres, so an unpinned ranged range would sit exactly on it. row: true: it is a wide row, not one arc, so the flight check does not sample a centre arc. needs: either launcher fires (a wall needs at least one; the halves and the gap are the wall block and wallSlots in src/foamers/wall.ts).

F06._note: GAME-10c: the Floater. It has no legs and no head: it floats (see float), so the leg handicaps do not apply and its turn rate is the no-head half of this one. attackRange is the reach of a spit; the blobs fly from there. preferredDistanceMetres is the ring it keeps, retreatDistanceMetres how close the player must get before it backs off.

float._note: GAME-10c: the float. hoverMetres: feet metres over the floor under it. bobMetres: the visual bob on top. damagedHoverMetres and damagedSpeedShare: the height and the speed share once a fin is lost; with no fins left it sits on the floor. fins: the parts that hold it up (the tendrils are decoration).

blob._note: GAME-10c: the blobs. A spit fires count small blobs fanned across spreadDeg degrees; they bounce off geometry bounces times before bursting, and there are never more than maxLive of any blob live. everyFourth: every fourth attack (counting the spits it actually fires) is the big pink blob instead: slower and bigger, and parryable like the Roamer's ball. speed m/s, gravity m/s2, radius and lifetime the ball's own, chunks at the burst.

mouth._note: GAME-10c: the weak point. The jaw drops to spit; while it is open (the windup and the strike) a dart on the jaw takes damage times the usual. Shut, it is an ordinary part.

F10._note: GAME-10j: the Turbo. On the Roamer's brain (see the F06), a ring it keeps at preferredDistanceMetres. Health 30 and speed 3.5 come from the rig. It flies on its jets (fly, the float's path); with one gone it flies lower and slower, with both gone it is on the floor walking. The jets are the weak points (weakpoint). The shot's numbers (homing): slow, light, and it steers at the player's chest for its seconds at its turn rate.

fly._note: GAME-10j: the jet flight. hoverMetres: feet metres over the floor under it, higher than the F06's. bobMetres: the visual bob on top. damagedHoverMetres and damagedSpeedShare: once a jet is lost; with no jets left it is on the floor walking (its legs). fins: the parts that hold it up, its jets; the wings are decoration. Same shape as the float the F06 uses.

homing._note: GAME-10j: the homing shot's ball. Slower and lighter than a thrown ball (the base spec's ball); it steers toward the player's chest for `seconds` at `turnDegPerSecond` (the step never turns more than that times dt) and then flies straight. A parry kills the steer on the player (the parry's own steer takes over). maxLive is the cap: not more than this many in the air.

weakpoint._note: GAME-10j: CONTENT-PLAN 3.1, the jets are the weak points. A dart on one takes damage x damage.

attacks._note: GAME-10j: one homing ball from the blaster tip (the ball's numbers are `homing` above). With the blaster gone, chooseAttack falls through to the bonk.

F11._note: GAME-10k: the Seawall. A 3.4 m armoured knight (CONTENT-PLAN 3.3): it walks in like the F01 (the melee brain), slow, and its shield is armour on the shield and shieldBoss parts across the front arc: a dart inside it does no damage and carves nothing, and darts can never break it. Darts from the side or back hit as usual. Health 60 and speed 1.4 come from the rig. Stage 1 keeps a plain bonk; the three-hit combo comes in stage 2.

armour._doc: GAME-10k: the tower shield (the weak point, orange). Inside its arcDeg front a dart is turned away whole: no damage, no carve. It is never broken by darts; only the finisher's parries break it (stage 2).

promoted._note: LVL-04b: a promoted spawn (the Ring's mini-boss pair). healthMultiplier scales the rig's health, so a Darter goes from 30 to 45. parts is per type id, then part id, then the voxel material that part wears instead of the rig's; Paul (2026-11-07) gives a promoted Darter light purple chest and brow plates. Never orange, pink, blue or yellow: those mean weak point, parryable and the player's darts.
